questions.a: 'sings beautifully' — the word modifies the verb 'sings', so it must be an adverb. A wrong answer keeping 'beautiful' shows the student doesn't apply the modifies-what test.

questions.q: 'He works ___ all day.' hard or hardly?
questions.a: 'hard' — works with effort. 'Hardly' = almost not ('He hardly works' = almost never works) — a wrong answer shows the trap pair isn't learned as separate words.
Adjective — 'a friendly dog'. It cannot be an adverb despite the -ly (the adverb form is 'in a friendly way'). A wrong answer 'adverb' shows the -ly-test is being trusted blindly.

questions.q: ______ describe nouns (a TALL building), adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs (runs QUICKLY, VERY tall, quite quickly).
Fill in the blank: Adjectives describe nouns (a TALL ______), adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs (runs QUICKLY, VERY tall, quite quickly).
Fill in the blank: The job test: ask 'what does it describe?' 'A quick runner' — quick describes the noun (______). 'She runs quickly' — quickly describes the verb (adverb).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student identifies what a modifier modifies, forms adverbs correctly (quick→quickly, easy→easily), uses good/well and hard/hardly correctly, and avoids double adverbials.
